issues.legal_issue: Civil court jurisdiction over a civil dispute is excluded when a statute gives finality to a competent special tribunal’s decision and provides an adequate alternative remedy, unless the tribunal failed to comply with the statute or fundamental principles of judicial procedure.
material_facts: A civil suit sought a declaration about whether the property was subject to a public or charitable trust or endowment.
The statute empowered a Deputy Commissioner to determine whether property was an endowment and provided a route to challenge that determination by suit or appeal.
The Deputy Commissioner followed the prescribed procedure, and there was no allegation that the Deputy Commissioner acted contrary to the statute or fundamental principles of judicial procedure.
issues.conclusion: The statutory scheme and the unchallenged order made by the Deputy Commissioner precluded the civil court from reopening the issue; the High Court’s decision did not call for interference.
issues.legal_principle: Section 9 of the Code of Civil Procedure presumes civil-court jurisdiction over suits of a civil nature, and exclusion is not readily inferred. Under Dhulabhai & Ors. v. State of Madhya Pradesh & Anr., 1968 (3) SCR 662, where a statute gives finality to a special tribunal’s orders, civil-court jurisdiction is excluded if an adequate remedy is available for the matters ordinarily addressed in a civil suit. Exclusion does not apply where the statute was not complied with or the tribunal did not follow fundamental principles of judicial procedure. Here, Sections 77 and 78 of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act provided for the determination and challenge of the endowment question.

rule.if: civil_suit and special_tribunal_has_final_decision and adequate_alternative_remedy and tribunal_followed_required_procedure

predicates.civil_suit: A party brought a civil suit to obtain a decision on a civil dispute.
predicates.special_tribunal_has_final_decision: A special tribunal made a decision on the issue in dispute, and that decision attained finality under the applicable statutory scheme.
predicates.adequate_alternative_remedy: The statutory scheme provided an adequate route for an aggrieved party to challenge the tribunal’s decision.
predicates.tribunal_followed_required_procedure: The tribunal followed the required procedure, and no failure to comply with the governing law or fundamental principles of judicial procedure was alleged.

issues.definition: When a civil suit concerns an issue finally decided by a special tribunal, an adequate statutory challenge route was available, and the tribunal followed the required procedure, the civil court cannot reopen that issue.

issues.legal_issue: An unchallenged final determination by a competent statutory authority that property is not an endowment is conclusive on that issue in a later civil proceeding concerning the same property.
material_facts: The Deputy Commissioner considered whether the property was a public charity or endowment and declared that it was not.
The order addressed the same question about the property’s status that was raised in the civil suit.
No suit or appeal challenging the order was filed through the route provided by the statute.
issues.conclusion: The Deputy Commissioner’s unchallenged order concluded the issue whether the property was a charitable or religious endowment and was final and conclusive.
issues.legal_principle: Section 77(1)(d) of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act empowered the Deputy Commissioner to determine whether property was an endowment and, if so, whether it was a charitable or religious endowment. Section 78 provided a route for an aggrieved person to challenge that determination by suit. Because the same issue was determined by the competent authority and no statutory challenge was brought, the order was conclusive.

rule.if: civil_suit and statutory_authority_decided_property_status and later_proceeding_concerns_same_issue and statutory_challenge_not_filed

predicates.civil_suit: A party brought a civil suit concerning the status of property.
predicates.statutory_authority_decided_property_sta: A competent statutory authority determined whether the property was an endowment or charitable or religious property.
predicates.later_proceeding_concerns_same_issue: The civil proceeding concerned the same property-status issue decided by the statutory authority.
predicates.statutory_challenge_not_filed: No challenge was brought through the statutory route provided for contesting the authority’s determination.

issues.definition: If a civil suit concerns the same property-status issue that a competent statutory authority decided, and no statutory challenge was filed, that determination is conclusive on the issue.

issues.legal_issue: A civil suit filed before a later statutory determination cannot be treated as the statutory suit for challenging that determination.
material_facts: The civil suit was filed before the proceeding in which the Deputy Commissioner made the order.
The statutory proceeding and order arose while the civil suit was pending.
A party contended that the pending civil suit could be construed as the statutory suit challenging the order.
issues.conclusion: The pending civil suit could not be treated as a suit under Section 78 because it preceded the statutory proceeding and order.
issues.legal_principle: Section 78 of the Andhra Pradesh Charitable and Hindu Religious Institutions and Endowments Act provided a suit as a means of challenging an order made under Section 77. A suit brought before the Section 77 proceeding and order cannot constitute the statutory challenge to that later order.

predicates.civil_suit: A party brought a civil suit concerning the issue later decided by a statutory authority.
predicates.existing_suit_predated_statutory_order: The civil suit was filed before the statutory authority made its order on that issue.
predicates.existing_suit_sought_to_challenge_later_: A party sought to rely on the already-filed suit as the statutory proceeding for challenging the later order.

issues.definition: A civil suit filed before a statutory order cannot serve as the statutory challenge to that later order, even if a party seeks to rely on it for that purpose.
